name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Long the current cross-sectional momentum leaders in software/semis/fintech, short two persistent laggards, with per-name stops - betting winners keep winning and losers keep losing.

positions.thesis: Raised 8->12, now the largest long. Last week I sized it at 8 because it was one metric short of a clean sweep, closing 1.6% below its 50-day; that gap has closed. It moved from 84.1% to 92.1% of its 52-week range in a week when the whole software cohort fell and it kept the best pure-software 12-1 momentum in my universe at +94.9%, at 38 realized vol against CRWD's 52. It reported 07-29 and does not print again until late October, so it carries the mandate's momentum exposure with none of the event risk I am paying to remove elsewhere. I am aware the sell side rates it Hold with a target below spot and that it fell 3.92% Friday — this mandate is built on cross-sectional momentum, not analyst targets, and one down day in a down tape does not touch the ranking. Stop -20%, capping the leg at 2.4% of NAV.

Raised 8->12. I bought this last week precisely because it passed every leg while the cohort broke down around it, and it then did the thing that claim predicts: 80.3% -> 87.1% of range on the week, with 12-1 momentum of +83.3% and record Q2 revenue and profit behind it. It reported 08-06 with nothing until late October, and it is my only communications-infrastructure exposure, so adding here concentrates conviction without concentrating theme — this is not a third way to own security. Sized to 12 rather than higher because 52 realized vol is the highest among my longs; the -24% stop is about a week and a half of sigma, wide enough not to be triggered by ordinary movement, and caps the leg at 2.9% of NAV.

Raised 7->10. Last week I argued NET was a name pulling back inside an uptrend rather than one breaking, and distinguished it from CRWD on that basis; it has now recovered from 77.9% to 81.3% of range while the cohort fell further, which is the confirmation of that distinction. Reported 08-06 with FedRAMP High certification and analyst upgrades behind the print and no event until late October. The add is three points rather than five because its 12-1 momentum remains middling relative to FTNT and TWLO, so it still earns its slot on breadth within the mandate rather than on conviction. Stop -22% caps it at 2.2% of NAV.

Halved 18->9 for the print on 09-02, and only for the print. The screen still loves it — 93.8% of its 52-week range is the best reading among my longs and it was the only long that rose in last week's rout. What I cannot defend is 18% of NAV on a coin flip where the stop cannot protect me: a -22% stop is inert against an overnight gap, so size is the only control I have, and I have no edge in forecasting a quarter. The setup is uncomfortably balanced — consensus target $327.85 against a $328.00 close means the sell side sees exactly zero upside, on 156x forward with no valuation floor to land on, which is the same reason I refused to press this at 18 last week. Half the position keeps the momentum expression and the drift I would want to own if the print is good; the other half stops being a bet on something I cannot handicap.

Untraded at 9 for a second week, and the honest reason is that it is neither good enough to add to nor broken enough to cut. It has slipped to 71.8% of its 52-week range, the weakest reading among my longs and 26% below its June high, and the supply-shortage story I originally wrote is still being argued with by Samsung and SK Hynix capacity additions. Against that, its 12-1 momentum of +756% remains the top reading in my universe by a factor of three and Nvidia continues to name memory as the binding constraint. It reports 09-30, safely outside this window, so it is not part of the event problem I am solving this week and there is no calendar reason to touch it. The wide -30% stop stays because 59% vol makes anything tighter noise; a full stop-out costs 2.7% of NAV.

Halved 15->8 for the 09-01 print. Note that I am cutting a position whose screen reading got BETTER — 85.0% -> 89.5% of range on the week despite -2.94% Friday, with 12-1 of +77.6% — which is the point: this is a calendar decision, not a ranking decision. Two things make the print asymmetric against a large position. The stock closed at $371.59 against a $364.01 consensus target, so it is already trading through where the sell side thinks it should be, on 95x forward; and China's security review is an unresolved negative that a guidance call can crystallise. At 8% a 10% adverse gap costs 0.8% of NAV instead of 1.5%. I keep the position because I want to own the momentum after the event, and I would rather re-size it next week with the print in hand than pay to guess it now.

Raised 6->8. I opened this as the honest consequence of covering COIN — the right answer to being wrong on a factor's direction is to stop fighting it — and it has held that ground, 91.3% of its 52-week range after a 1.5% down day in a down week, above its 10-, 50- and 200-day, with record Q2 profitability and raised guidance behind it. It reported 08-05 and has no event in the window, which is exactly what I am buying more of this week. The add is two points rather than five because the weak part of the case has not changed: 12-1 momentum of +3.2% is thin, and thin 12-1 is the reason this is a moderate position and not a conviction one. It remains my only long expression of the fintech leg the mandate names.

Upsized 5->6, the only position in this book where the week's macro news is unambiguously in my favour. It fell 4.6% to 9.6% of its 52-week range — now the lowest reading in my universe, below both its 50- and 200-day, with 12-1 momentum of -56.6% — and it did that in the same week that the Fed chair put rate hikes back on the table, which lands directly on an unsecured consumer lender's funding costs and credit box. It reported 08-04, so unlike ORCL it carries no event in this window, which is why this is the short I am adding to rather than the one I am cutting. The add is one point, not three: I know the fundamentals are good — 50% origination growth, conditional OCC bank approval, a $4B Castlelake forward-flow — and that is precisely the squeeze risk, so 6% at 65 realized vol with a wide -30% stop caps the leg at 1.8% of NAV.

Halved 6->3, and this is a correction of my own error. I upsized this last week explicitly on the reasoning that earnings were around 09-10 and therefore outside the window; the print is 09-04, inside it. Two things follow. First, the confirmation I upsized on has weakened — ORCL rose about 1% in a week the S&P fell 1.4%, so it is no longer failing to participate. Second, the squeeze setup into the event is the worst in my book: consensus sees 62% upside, Citi has an open positive catalyst watch at $330, and a strong AI-backlog number could gap it violently through a -20% stop that cannot fill on an overnight move. The laggard case is still the best on my screen — 15.7% of range, 12-1 of -47.9%, -$23.7B free cash flow, $97.6B net debt, BBB- one notch off junk with roughly $40B of FY27 financing needed into a market that just repriced toward hikes — so I keep the short at a size where being wrong through the print costs well under a point of NAV, and I will re-size it once the number is public.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: I re-checked every earnings date instead of trusting my own notes and found an error that changes the week: PANW prints 09-01, SNOW 09-02 and ORCL 09-04 — all three inside this window, not two of them. Last week I wrote that ORCL reported ~09-10 and was outside the window; that was wrong, and I am correcting it rather than carrying a short into a catalyst I told myself was not there. At last week's weights that is 39% of the book on binary events in four sessions, in an account already -2.62% with a -7.73% drawdown. The decisive argument is mechanical: my per-name stops, which are the stated risk control of this entire mandate, do not function through an overnight earnings gap — a -22% stop on SNOW is worthless if it opens -18%. For an event inside the window, size is the only control that exists. My edge is cross-sectional momentum, not predicting prints, so I halve the three event positions (SNOW 18->9, PANW 15->8, ORCL short 6->3) and keep every thesis intact. This is not a flinch on the screens: SNOW is still my best range read at 93.8% and PANW actually IMPROVED to 89.5% of range this week. The freed capital goes to the names that pass the same screen and have no print until late October and therefore express the mandate cleanly — FTNT 8->12 (92.1% of range, up from 84.1%, best pure-software 12-1 in my universe), TWLO 8->12 (87.1%, up from 80.3%), NET 7->10 (81.3%, up from 77.9%), XYZ 6->8 — and UPST goes 5->6 because it is the only leg where the macro news is unambiguously in my favour: a hike-risk repricing hits an unsecured consumer lender's funding costs directly, and it fell to 9.6% of its 52-week range, the lowest reading in my universe, with no event in the window. MU stays at 9 unchanged — no print until 09-30, but at 71.8% of range with the supply story contested it has not earned an add. Cash 18->23 is the residue of stepping out of event risk, not a market call.
novelty: This book shares no instrument and no factor with my Round-2 breadth basket — Round 2 is long equal-weight, small-cap, energy, biotech and materials index exposure against a QQQ index short, while Round 3 is single-name cross-sectional momentum in software, memory and fintech against two single-name laggard shorts, so same-direction gross-weight overlap is zero; the two books also now diverge in what drove this week's decision, since Round 2 was rebalanced on deteriorating sector range readings and Round 3 was rebalanced on an earnings-calendar correction that no index position in Round 2 is exposed to.
research_notes:
MACRO — the regime input changed this week and it is not my own chart inference this time. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address stated that "inflation is running too high"; markets repriced toward rate HIKES rather than cuts. S&P 500 -1.4% on the week, snapping a three-week win streak; Friday S&P -0.25%, Nasdaq -0.52%, Dow flat. Gold -2.88% and Bitcoin -2.29% to ~$77.6k on Friday, i.e. the classic liquidity-tightening repricing. VIX only 14.43, so this is a repricing, not a panic. This matters because a hike-risk regime lands hardest on exactly the cohorts my Round-2 breadth mandate owns (small caps, regional banks, leveraged small-cap) and on the long-duration high-multiple software my Round-3 mandate owns, while it is a tailwind to both of my Round-3 shorts (ORCL: -$23.7B FCF, $97.6B net debt, ~$40B FY27 financing need; UPST: unsecured consumer lender funding costs).

ROUND-2 PRICE READINGS (52-wk range %, 08-28 close, prior week in brackets): RSP 93.3 [97.4], IWM 87.6 [93.7], XLE 91.0 [99.5], XBI 90.7 [95.3], XLB 91.7 [100.0], TNA 81.9 [90.0], KRE 80.5 [85.3], XLI 73.1 [84.3], QQQ 83.3 [83.0]. Every long deteriorated; nothing broke. Two readings stand out: XLI has now fallen for a second straight week and is the worst sector read I own, and TNA lost roughly 4.5% against IWM's 1.5% — the 3x daily-compounding drag I have flagged three weeks running, now in a tape with a fresh reason to chop. The RSP/QQQ concentration spread went slightly against me for the first time in three weeks (QQQ roughly flat, RSP -0.8%), which is what a hawkish repricing does: cash-rich mega-cap beats leveraged small-cap. ETH $2,434.86, sitting at the low end of a $2,409-$2,526 seven-day range — the CLARITY Act / melt-up bounce has stalled and BTC has rolled over, so the catalyst I refused to chase has now passed.

ROUND-3 — THE FINDING THAT DRIVES THIS WEEK. I checked every earnings date rather than trusting last week's notes, and one of them was wrong. Three of my nine positions print INSIDE the coming window: PANW Tue 09-01, SNOW Wed 09-02, and ORCL Fri 09-04. I wrote last week that ORCL reports "~09-10, outside the window"; that is factually incorrect. At current weights that is 18+15+6 = 39% of the book on binary events in four sessions, in an account already -2.62% with a -7.73% max drawdown. Setups: SNOW $328.00, 93.8% of range, consensus PT $327.85 — the stock is exactly at target, 156x forward, no valuation floor. PANW $371.59, 89.5% of range [85.0], -2.94% Friday, consensus PT $364.01 — trading ABOVE target, 95x forward, China security review still live. ORCL $150.85, 15.7% of range [15.0] — it stopped underperforming and ticked up ~1% in a -1.4% tape, so the non-participation confirmation I upsized on has weakened, and it goes into a print with 62% consensus upside and a Citi positive-catalyst-watch $330 target. Names with NO print in the window improved their readings while the cohort fell: FTNT 92.1 [84.1], TWLO 87.1 [80.3], NET 81.3 [77.9], XYZ 91.3 [93.0], and my best short UPST fell to 9.6% of range [12.3], -4.6% on the week, the lowest reading in my universe. MU $932.86 is 71.8% of range [77.5] with earnings 09-30 (outside window) and the supply-shortage story still contested by Samsung/SK Hynix additions.

THE GOVERNING POINT: a stop-loss does not work through an earnings gap. A -22% stop on SNOW is worthless if it opens -18%. For an event inside the window the only risk control that exists is position size, and my mandate is cross-sectional momentum, not event trading — I have no edge in a single-name print. So I cut event size and redeploy into the momentum names that carry no event.
